card.name: Commas after drug-class warning clauses
card.fires_on: A comma that ends a clause about a drug or drug class in warning text, just before a qualifier such as 'if treatment is discontinued' or 'including [brand]'. Also fires on the noun after an adverse-event adjective, such as 'systolic dysfunction' or 'anaphylactic reactions'.

modes.label: Comma after remit clause
modes.description: Comma after 'may remit, partially or completely' in tardive dyskinesia text, before an 'if treatment is stopped' clause.
modes.example: Tardive dyskinesia may remit, partially or completely<<,>> if antipsychotic treatment is discontinued

modes.label: Comma after drug class
modes.description: Comma after a drug or class name in a safety statement, before 'including' or a result clause.
modes.example: have been reported with interferon beta products<<,>> including REBIF.

modes.label: Adverse-event noun
modes.description: The noun completing a named adverse event, such as dysfunction or reactions.
modes.example: Severe, sometimes fatal, anaphylactic<< reactions>> to NSAIDs have been reported in such

card.writes: It suppresses words like outcome and results, so the text after the comma is steered away from stating outcomes.
card.plain: It marks the comma in a warning sentence where a condition or example list comes next, not an outcome.
